html:
Ryazan was a Russian principality on the Oka river, south-east of Moscow, on the edge of the open steppe. It split off from Chernigov in the 1100s and lasted until Moscow absorbed it in 1521. On the 1279 and 1300 maps its shape is drawn far too large; in 1492 and 1500 it is the small state it really was.

As a frontier land it took the first blows from the steppe. In December 1237 the Mongols under Batu Khan stormed Old Ryazan and destroyed it, the opening of the Mongol invasion of Rus. The old city never recovered, and the capital moved to the town that now bears the name Ryazan.

Under the Golden Horde Ryazan was a rival of the rising Moscow. Its prince Oleg kept apart from the Russian side at the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380. Moscow's grip tightened over the next century, and Vasili III annexed it in 1521.
